vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gateway-restart-profiler
Version: 0.1.1

The skill is a performance profiling tool for the OpenClaw Gateway that analyzes startup logs to identify bottlenecks. The bash script (gateway-profile.sh) monitors the gateway restart process, calculates durations for various initialization stages, and generates a visual HTML report using Chart.js. The logic is transparent and aligns with the stated purpose in SKILL.md, with no evidence of data exfiltration, persistence, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's Linux bash script largely matches its stated purpose (profiling gateway restart by reading local logs and generating an HTML report), but there are small inconsistencies (promised Windows script missing, some documented output paths/text not matched by the script) and it will stop/start the gateway which is disruptive — review before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to analyze OpenClaw Gateway restart performance; the included scripts/gateway-profile.sh actively stops/starts the gateway, tails/parses local openclaw log files, and generates reports — which is coherent with the stated purpose. However the SKILL.md advertises Windows (PowerShell) support while no PowerShell script (gateway-profile.ps1) is present in the package. SKILL.md also mentions saving text summaries to a temp directory, while the script writes HTML/text output to ~/.openclaw/logs; these mismatches reduce completeness.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime behavior is local: it searches for openclaw-*.log under ~/.openclaw/logs or /tmp, invokes 'openclaw gateway stop' and 'openclaw gateway start' (disruptive actions), tails/parses log lines, computes phase durations, and writes reports to the user's home directory. It does not appear to transmit parsed data to external endpoints, but the generated HTML pulls Chart.js from a public CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net). The agent running this skill will therefore have permission to stop/start the gateway and read local logs — expected for profiling but potentially disruptive and sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with a bundled script). That minimizes installer risk. The HTML report references Chart.js from a public CDN (network fetch when opening the HTML), which is an external dependency but not an installer concern. The script itself is local and not downloaded at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials and doesn't access unrelated secrets. It relies on standard runtime context (HOME, /tmp) and on the presence of the 'openclaw' CLI in PATH and 'bc' for numeric formatting — reasonable for a local gateway profiling tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-enabled (always:false) and does not modify other skills or system-wide configs. It writes reports under the user's ~/.openclaw/logs and uses temporary files; these are scoped to the user. The major privilege is the ability to stop/start the gateway process, which is expected for a restart profiler but should be considered operationally sensitive.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing/running:
- Review the script before running. It will run 'openclaw gateway stop' and 'openclaw gateway start' (it will stop and restart your gateway), so do not run it against production instances without scheduling downtime.
- The package claims Windows (PowerShell) support, but no PowerShell script is included — Windows behavior is not provided here. If you need Windows support, ask the author for gateway-profile.ps1.
- The script reads local log files (~/.openclaw/logs or /tmp/openclaw). Ensure those logs are accessible and you are comfortable allowing this tool to read them.
- The generated HTML loads Chart.js from a public CDN (jsdelivr). If you require no external network access or want to avoid third-party CDN requests, host Chart.js locally or inspect/modify the HTML template.
- Run it as the same user who owns the gateway process; avoid running as root unless necessary. Consider testing in a staging environment first.
- If you have concerns about sensitive content in logs (tokens, API keys), inspect the log files first or run the profiler on a sanitized copy of the logs.
- If you want higher assurance, request the missing PowerShell script and ask the author to document exactly which 'openclaw' CLI and log formats are required. If anything looks unexpected or the script tries to contact remote hosts beyond the Chart.js CDN, do not run it.
